description: Human alterations of the global floodplains 1992–2019 is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by Adnan Rajib et al. Floodplains provide critical ecosystem services; however, loss of natural floodplain functions caused by human alterations increase flood risks and lead to massive loss of life and property. Despite recent calls for improved floodplain protection and management, a global-scale assessment quantifying human floodplain alterations does not exist. Coverage: global; published in 2023. Formats: XML, GeoTIFF, Excel, ZIP, PDF. The data are held in Consortium of Universities for the Advancement of Hydrologic Science, Inc and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Size stated by the repository: 7228957691 bytes. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is This resource is shared under the Creative Commons Attribution CC BY., taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support multi-sector infrastructure risk and planning studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
